body: Any car must look manufactured and real: symmetric body with consistent panel gaps, four round wheels with the right tyre size and rims, readable badge in the right place, correct number of doors and mirrors, headlights and grille shaped as the real model, reflective paint with sky and surroundings in it, a believable licence plate (Iraqi plates: white with black numbers and the governorate name in Arabic), interior visible through glass.

Toyota Land Cruiser (the Iraqi favourite): big boxy full-size SUV, tall upright grille with the Toyota oval logo, large square headlights, wide flared wheel arches, side steps, often white or black and polished, tinted windows; inside: leather seats, wood trim, a big touchscreen. Shown cruising on a highway or parked in front of a villa.

Toyota Hilux pickup: double cab with an open load bed at the back, rugged bumper, raised suspension, often white and dusty, used for work and farms – load bed with boxes, gas cylinders or watermelons, sometimes with a canvas cover.

Baghdad taxi: a compact sedan (Kia, Hyundai or Saipa) painted white with orange or yellow side panels or roof sign, slightly worn, a prayer bead hanging from the mirror, the driver's arm out of the window; minibuses (كيا كوستر) for shared rides with a conductor calling the route.

Iraqi tuk-tuk: three-wheeled motor rickshaw, small cabin with a canvas or metal roof, often decorated with stickers, LED lights, flags and Arabic phrases, a single headlight, buzzing engine; weaving through traffic in Baghdad neighbourhoods.

Luxury and sports cars exactly as the brand looks: the correct grille (Mercedes three-pointed star, BMW kidney grille, Rolls-Royce Pantheon grille and Spirit of Ecstasy, Lexus spindle grille, Porsche round headlights and sloping roof, Ferrari prancing-horse badge and low red body, Lamborghini sharp angular wedge); deep glossy paint with crisp reflections, low stance, big alloy wheels with brake callipers visible.

Motorcycle: two wheels in line with a visible engine, exhaust, handlebars with mirrors and levers, the rider leaning into turns with knees gripping the tank, a helmet; delivery scooters with a box on the back are common in Iraqi cities.

Bus: long body with many windows in a row, doors that fold open, a destination sign above the windscreen; Baghdad red double-decker buses for city lines, white Kia Coaster minibuses for shared routes, passengers visible through the windows.

Truck: a heavy cab with a big grille, many wheels on several axles, a long trailer or tipper, mud flaps, a dusty body; it moves slowly with weight, the trailer swaying slightly, air brakes hiss when it stops.

Airliner done right: a long tube fuselage with a row of small windows, two swept wings with engines hanging under them, a tall tail fin with the airline livery (Iraqi Airways: white with green and the airline logo on the tail), landing gear with multiple wheels; takeoff: it rolls faster, the nose lifts first, then climbs with the gear retracting; airports: jet bridges, terminal glass, apron vehicles.

Helicopter: a cabin with a big main rotor on top and a small tail rotor, rotor blades blur into a disc when spinning (motion blur), downwash flattens grass and throws dust in a circle, a heavy rhythmic thudding sound.

Train: a locomotive at the front with connected carriages behind, steel wheels on two rails with sleepers and gravel, the train sways slightly, wheels clack over rail joints, a horn blows; stations with platforms, overhead signs and waiting passengers.

Boats: a boat sits in the water with part of the hull submerged, bobs and rolls gently, leaves a V-shaped wake when moving; marsh mashoof (مشحوف): a long narrow black wooden canoe pushed with a pole through reeds; yachts: white glossy hull, deck, chrome rails; cargo ships at Umm Qasr: containers stacked in colours.

Bicycle: two equal wheels with spokes, a diamond frame, chain to the rear gear, pedals on cranks, a saddle and handlebars with brake levers; it must be mechanically correct with the chain connected and pedals opposite each other.
Farm tractor: large rear wheels with deep treads and small front wheels, an exhaust pipe puffing smoke, a cab or open seat, pulling a plough or trailer through a field, dust and soil behind it.
